subject: Teaches controlled classification systems for categories, facets, browse taxonomies, SKOS broader/narrower links,…

evals.prompt: Define taxonomy-design in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the taxonomy-design skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind taxonomy-design. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.
A user asks: "define OWL class restrictions and property domains for this knowledge base". Should taxonomy-design activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force taxonomy-design onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to skill-infrastructure, information-architecture, context-graph, canonical-repo-structure, conceptual-modeling, ontology-modeling, knowledge-modeling, semantic-relations.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "our skill categories are drifting: some are by domain, some by activity, and some by tool - how should the taxonomy be redesigned?". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying taxonomy-design.

Place taxonomy-design among its adjacent skills (skill-infrastructure, information-architecture, context-graph, canonical-repo-structure, conceptual-modeling, ontology-modeling, knowledge-modeling, semantic-relations). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about taxonomy-design and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
